text:
Oliver: Heads up — during a long-context stress run I hit steady GPU memory growth that never dropped even after the request finished. Looks like our KV paging/page-table state isn't releasing pages. :bug:

Chen: Which rig / model? This sounds like the PagedAttention-style behavior we saw before.

Oliver: Reproducer: run long-streamer with batch_size=1 seq_len=131k on llamax-8b quantized. Observed on both A100 (ampere) and H100 (hopper) but with different symptoms: A100 shows ~20% fragmentation (lots of small free segments), H100 shows page-table entries stuck in 'resident' but pages not in any arena.

Sasha: Can you paste profiler output? kernel timings / memcpy logs are helpful.

Oliver: Paste from the debug trace (trimmed):
```
[KV-PAGE] alloc_page arena=3 page_id=0x7f9b1f00 size=64KB -> GPU 0
[KV-PAGE] map_page pte_idx=12015 -> resident=1
[KV-EVICT] candidate pte_idx=12015 last_used=1719000100
[KV-EVICT] eviction failed: refcount>0
[KV-LEAK] orphaned pte_idx=12015 arena=3
... memory_growth: +1.2GB over 1000 steps
```
Notes: eviction attempted but refcount still positive (should have been cleared). The page-table still points to the GPU address even though arena free list claims the block free -> double-booking.

Maya: That looks like the bug we tried to repro in 2024 Q4 (PR #3412). Did the rollback reintroduce it?

Oliver: I traced to commit 6b2c9f1 (kernel-selection/batching refactor). The bug is subtle: when we migrate pages between arenas during compact/merge, we update the arena free list but don't atomically update the page-table 'owner' pointer under the same lock on Hopper path because of a different CUDA mempool we use there. On Ampere we get lucky because the race window is small.

Chen: So non-atomic ownership update -> PTE still points to old slot -> allocator later reuses that slot and we end up with two references. That explains refcount>0 on eviction. Any repro that flips a bit into consistent failure mode?

Oliver: Yes, run `kv_paged_smash --num_alloc=20000 --steal=concurrent` under H100 drivers 535.x and you get deterministic orphaned pages after ~500 steps. I've attached a small unit test in the branch `oliver/kv-pagetable-fix` that reliably reproduces.

Sasha: Thanks. Quick triage: is this limited to PagedAttention work (our custom paging code) or affects general KV cache codepath?

Oliver: Primarily PagedAttention path because it does aggressive page migrations/compaction to keep GPU L2 pressure low. But any codepath that does cross-arena moves without atomic PTE update can hit it.

Maya: Impact? Customer-facing?

Oliver: Risky for long-context customers on Dedicated / Private where sequences can be >100k tokens. Observed OOMs or silent memory leak growth leading to degraded throughput. Hosted API less likely because shorter sequences and frequent restarts.

infra-bot: nightly-kv-stress (job 2026-03-16-03) finished: failed (flaky) — 3/10 failed reproducer; logs at https://ci.internal/jobs/12345

Chen: I'll review the test and the patch. My plan: add an atomic swap for the PTE update and hold the arena lock until both structures updated. Also add assert sanity-check in debug builds to ensure no double-booking.

Sasha: Can you also add a diagnostic that dumps PTEs with refcount>0 but whose owner is on free list? That will help catch regressions in nightly runs.

Chen: Yep. Also want to run it across both driver stacks (535.x and 545.x) and both GPUs. H100 does a different mempool path so we need driver coverage.

Maya: If patch looks safe, we should cherry-pick to the 2.1.x maintenance branch (we're seeing it in prod Dedicated customers). Add a small rollback-safe flag gated behind `KV_PAGETABLE_STRICT_UPDATES` to toggle on/off until patch lands in edge.

Oliver: I put a minimal patch at https://git.internal/r/redwood/infra/+/r4587 (WIP). It passes unit tests locally.

Chen: I'll run integration on both GPU types now. If green I'll open the PR and request 2 approvals.

Sasha: Adding perf note — after atomic update, watch for any extra stalls around compaction because we held lock longer. We might need to change compaction heuristics to avoid long critical sections. Maybe do handoff: create new page, pteswap, then reclaim old page outside critical path.

Oliver: Good call. I'll prototype a handoff approach that minimizes lock time.

Maya: Action items:
- Chen: finish PR + run CI across drivers (due EOD)
- Oliver: add handoff prototype + stress test (due EOD+1)
- Sasha: add diagnostics to nightly job and update perf dashboards

Oliver: For anyone debugging locally: quick commands —
```
# reproduce on a node
CUDA_VISIBLE_DEVICES=0 ./kv_paged_smash --len 131072 --driver 535 --log debug
# dump suspicious ptes
./kv_tool dump-pte --refcount-gt 0 --owner-free
```

Chen: I'll post PR link when ready. Thanks for the detailed repro, Oliver. :thumbsup:

Maya: Thanks team. Keep me posted if we need emergency rollback for any clusters.

Oliver: Will follow up with the exact stack traces and small perf numbers once I run the handoff experiment. :eyes:
